findings.title: Unrelated audit-log change enables unvetted advanced pagination for non-superusers
findings.body: This spans-buffer PR also switches the audit-log endpoint to OptimizedCursorPaginator when optimized_pagination=true is supplied and the caller is a superuser OR merely has organization_context.member.has_global_access. has_global_access is team-access scope for ordinary organization members, not proof of administrator/superuser status as the comment claims. This exposes a separate, user-controlled pagination implementation on a sensitive endpoint, unrelated to span buffering, and should be removed or reviewed/tested as its own API change.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering of its only caller
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. Its only caller orders AuditLogEntry by -datetime, for which DateTimePaginator is required: it converts epoch-millis cursor values to timezone-aware datetimes and formats item keys with strftime. With -datetime, build_queryset receives an integer instead of a datetime and build_cursor calls math.floor on a datetime, so the optimized audit-log path will raise TypeError/database comparison errors instead of returning a page.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing, which does not support them
findings.body: Cursor values and offsets come from the request query string and Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets. The optimized branch deliberately uses cursor.offset as the slice start when enable_advanced_features is set, and BasePaginator at line 182 likewise preserves negative offsets for is_prev cursors. The claim that Django ORM handles this is false: Django QuerySet slicing asserts 'Negative indexing is not supported', so a crafted cursor such as a negative-offset prev/next cursor produces a 500 rather than safely paging from the end. Pagination bounds need explicit validation/clamping before slicing.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts span end-timestamp scores on overlaps
findings.body: The old SUNIONSTORE deduplicated identical payloads without changing metadata. The new redis.call('zunionstore', set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) uses Redis' default AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both sorted sets (duplicate delivery, a merge of overlapping partial segments, or destination/source overlap) gets score roughly end_timestamp+end_timestamp instead of its end timestamp. That corrupts the score later used by zpopmin eviction, artificially protecting duplicated spans and causing other spans to be evicted first. Use an explicit AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) to preserve one real timestamp.

findings.title: SET-to-ZSET switch breaks in-flight Redis segments with WRONGTYPE errors
findings.body: Existing buffered segment keys were created as Redis SETs by sadd and can remain live until the one-hour redis_ttl/flush timeouts expire. This change immediately issues ZADD in process_spans, and the Lua script likewise issues ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN, while flush uses ZSCAN. Redis returns WRONGTYPE when a sorted-set command is used on an existing SET key, so during rollout process_spans fails for traces already buffered, batches retry/stall, and unflushed spans can be lost when the old keys expire. The PR contains no key versioning, drain, dual-type handling, or other migration for in-flight keys.

findings.title: Flush-time max_segment_spans guard removed while insert cap ignores the configured limit
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans; after this change that constructor setting is effectively dead. Eviction is instead hardcoded to 1000 in add-buffer.lua, so the default changes from 1001 to 1000 and any custom max_segment_spans value is silently ignored. Segments that bypass insert eviction, including pre-existing large segments, are now loaded and emitted regardless of span count, bounded only by max_segment_bytes, increasing memory and downstream segment-size risk.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The redirect-following loop previously allowed 10000 hops, with a comment acknowledging that deeper segment trees might not be joined correctly. Reducing it to 1000 makes that failure mode ten times more likely: when the cap is exhausted the script proceeds with an unresolved set_span_id and no error, so spans for a deep chain can be placed in a different segment key and flushed as split/incomplete segments rather than being joined to their root segment.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently drops spans with no metric or truncation signal
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, zpopmin permanently discards the earliest-ending spans during insert. Unlike the removed flush-time span-count guard, which emitted spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and logged the segment size, this path emits no metric/log and marks the flushed segment in no way as truncated. Operators cannot measure span loss and downstream consumers receive an incomplete segment indistinguishable from a complete one.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction, sorted-set merge, or score behavior
findings.body: The test changes only add the newly required end_timestamp_precise field to existing Span constructions. No test inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment, asserts which spans zpopmin retains, covers duplicate payloads across merged partial segments, or verifies that scores remain real end timestamps after ZUNIONSTORE. The central data-loss behavior introduced by this PR is therefore untested.
